chapter: Bird, the band's breakup and Luis Russell
title: Singers Hibler, Bill Nolan and Walter Brown
summary: Nolan sang ballads before Brown; Al Hibbler joined in San Antonio; Witherspoon came after Ramey left.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: When did you -- when did you pick up Hibler then?
We picked up Hibler in 1940 or either late 1940 or early 1941.
Well --
In San Antonio, Texas.
Well, did you have him and --
Brown --
Together?
And we had Bill Noland.
It must have --
See, we had -- we had Bill Noland, and he was singing the blues before we got Walter Brown.
Well, how well could he sing the
He just didn't have that nasty voice like Brown.
Yeah, but I mean could he sing?
He was a great ballad singer.
Oh.
So when we got Hibler, then he started -- you know, what's his name would just sing the blues. But he really didn't have the voice for the blues. He had a more or less a Pha Terrell voice.
Well, what did Hibler sing?
Well, Hibler sang -- he sang some blues too, but he sang the ballads.
Well, when does Witherspoon come in there?
Oh, that was after I left.
Oh.
But now, when we came to New York, we brought three singers. We brought Brown --
The first time?
Yeah, Bill Nolan and whats his name And McShann talked to Bill and told him it was too expensive. So and then Bill agreed to go on back to Kansas City.
